title: Trump: Semion Mogilevich, the ‘boss of bosses,' is born in Ukraine
description_short: Trump: Semion Mogilevich, the ‘boss of bosses,' is born in Ukraine
description_medium: Semion Mogilevich, born in Kyiv in 1946, was described by a 2014 Business Insider profile as a Russian crime figure and former money-laundering contact for the Solntsevskaya Bratva. The profile recounts FBI allegations about investor fraud and transnational criminal activity, and discusses a 1998 FBI assessment of his organization.
description_long: Born in Kyiv on June 30, 1946, Semion Mogilevich later became a Russian organized-crime figure whom the FBI placed on its Ten Most Wanted list, according to a 2014 Business Insider profile. The article describes him as a former money-laundering contact for the Solntsevskaya Bratva and says he used front companies and accounts in multiple countries. It recounts FBI allegations that he participated in a $150 million investor-fraud scheme involving YBM Magnex, a Canadian company. The profile also summarizes a 1998 FBI report that described an organization of about 250 members and alleged activities including arms dealing, trafficking in nuclear material, prostitution, drug trafficking, oil deals, and money laundering. FBI Special Agent Peter Kowenhoven described Mogilevich as dangerous because he operated across borders. Mogilevich denied wrongdoing in a BBC interview cited by the profile, saying authorities had to prove their claims.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Semion Mogilevich, the ‘boss of bosses,' is born in Ukraine
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Semion Mogilevich, the ‘boss of bosses,' is born in Ukraine

notes: needs_context: the Trump File timeline calls Mogilevich a Trump associate and fellow money launderer and dates the crime ring to 1994. Its linked Business Insider profile supports criminal-history details but does not document that Trump association or the claimed formation date.

title: Trump: Bob Levinson: The most dangerous people on Earth have reached the USA
description_short: Trump: Bob Levinson: The most dangerous people on Earth have reached the USA
description_medium: BBC Panorama’s 1999 program “The Billion Dollar Don” examined Russian crime figure Semion Mogilevich. Former FBI agent Bob Levinson described the criminal figures arriving in the United States as exceptionally wealthy and dangerous, and said Mogilevich could target people who obstructed him. The program centered on Mogilevich’s alleged organization.
description_long: The BBC transcript for Panorama’s “The Billion Dollar Don” centers on Semion Mogilevich and Russian organized crime. Former FBI special agent Bob Levinson, who worked on organized-crime investigations, described Mogilevich as a sophisticated racketeer and warned that people who stood in his way could become targets. The program’s presenter cited Russian Interior Ministry files that described Mogilevich as a crime boss and financier of prostitution, gambling, and money laundering; Mogilevich denied the allegations, saying there were no documents to prove them. FBI deputy assistant director Jim Moody described Mogilevich as educated and multilingual and said corruption linked to the operation reached into Russian government. Mogilevich told the program he had been selling wheat and grain. The episode presents law-enforcement assessments alongside Mogilevich’s denials and follows an investigation into alleged transnational racketeering. Levinson described a decade-long effort to pursue Mogilevich, continuing after he left the FBI.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Bob Levinson: The most dangerous people on Earth have reached the USA
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Bob Levinson: The most dangerous people on Earth have reached the USA

notes: needs_context: the BBC transcript confirms the quote comes from “The Billion Dollar Don,” about Semion Mogilevich, but does not mention Trump. Its text gives no interview date; the filename 06_12_99 is ambiguous against the Trump File timeline’s July 1, 1999 date, so the exact date and Trump connection remain unsubstantiated.

title: Trump: Saudi Prince Al-Waleed bin Talal gives Rudy Giuliani $10 million for 9/11
description_short: Trump: Saudi Prince Al-Waleed bin Talal gives Rudy Giuliani $10 million for 9/11
description_medium: On October 11, 2001, Prince Alwaleed bin Talal presented New York Mayor Rudy Giuliani with a $10 million check for the Twin Towers Fund. Giuliani announced he would not accept it after a press release attached to the prince’s condolence letter criticized U.S. policy in the Middle East. The prince later said the money was intended for victims’ families.
description_long: Contemporaneous New York Times reporting says Prince Alwaleed bin Talal presented New York Mayor Rudy Giuliani with a $10 million check for the Twin Towers Fund on October 11, 2001. Giuliani initially accepted the check with a condolence letter condemning terrorism. A separate press release attached to the letter criticized U.S. policy in the Middle East and urged a more balanced position on the Palestinian cause. Giuliani publicly rejected that statement and said the city would not accept the donation. Two days later, the prince said the money was intended for victims and their families and expressed regret that it had been refused, while maintaining his criticism of U.S. policy. The prince later explained that he had raised the Palestinian cause in response to reporters’ questions about how to address terrorism.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Saudi Prince Al-Waleed bin Talal gives Rudy Giuliani $10 million for 9/11
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Saudi Prince Al-Waleed bin Talal gives Rudy Giuliani $10 million for 9/11

notes: needs_context: archived New York Times reports confirm the $10 million Twin Towers Fund check and Giuliani’s rejection after the attached press release criticized U.S. policy; the prince later explained the political statement was meant to answer reporters. The contemporaneous accounts do not connect Trump to Giuliani’s decision. The Trump File page’s separate claim of a Trump–prince financial relationship is not corroborated in these reports.

title: Donald Trump signs Villa Trump deal with Elite pedophile's friend
description_short: Donald Trump signs Villa Trump deal with Elite pedophile's friend
description_medium: A New York Times report says Donald Trump met Brazilian entrepreneur Ricardo R. Bellino in January 2003 and agreed to a proposed resort carrying the Trump name near São Paulo. The $40 million Villa Trump plan included a golf course, hotel, spa, and homes. By May 2004, the report was still describing development and financing plans.
description_long: In a New York Times report published in May 2004, Brazilian entrepreneur Ricardo R. Bellino described pitching Donald Trump on a golf club and resort near São Paulo. Bellino said Trump agreed to the idea during a January 2003 meeting in Manhattan. The proposed $40 million Villa Trump development, planned for Itatiba about 55 miles from São Paulo, included an 18-hole golf course, hotel, spa, and as many as 500 memberships, some tied to home plots. The article reported that financing was expected from two Brazilian families and that the project would be separate from Trump Hotels and Casino Resorts. Bellino also recruited Jack Nicklaus to design the course, and Trump requested that Bill Clinton and several actors be honorary members. The Times reported that memberships were expected to cost $350,000 to $500,000 and that the 150 founding members would receive private cottages.

preserved_fields.title: Donald Trump signs Villa Trump deal with Elite pedophile's friend
preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump signs Villa Trump deal with Elite pedophile's friend

notes: needs_context: BBC’s linked article concerns Epstein’s birthday scrapbook and does not mention Villa Trump. The cited New York Times report confirms the January 2003 meeting and proposed partnership but not completion of the resort or the timeline’s claim that John Casablancas arranged the meeting.

title: Trump: Epstein & Maxwell traffic Florida mom, threaten to feed her to alligators

Her account describes alleged abuse and trafficking over several months, along with threats to use claimed influence over law enforcement against her family. These are allegations attributed to the plaintiff.

title: Donald Trump uses Trump Foundation to bribe Florida Attorney General
description_short: Donald Trump uses Trump Foundation to bribe Florida Attorney General
description_medium: A 2016 Washington Post report says the Trump Foundation made a $25,000 political contribution in 2013 while Florida Attorney General Pam Bondi was considering whether to investigate Trump University; Bondi later decided not to pursue the case. After questions about the filing, Trump corrected it, paid a $2,500 IRS penalty, and reimbursed the Foundation. The sequence alone does not establish an agreement.
description_long: A Washington Post report published in 2016 said the Donald J. Trump Foundation made a $25,000 contribution to a political group connected to Florida Attorney General Pam Bondi in 2013, while her office was considering fraud allegations involving Trump University. Bondi decided not to pursue the case. The Foundation had reported the money as a donation to a Kansas charity with a similar name, although the Post said that group received no payment. After the Post and a watchdog group raised questions, Trump filed corrected paperwork with the IRS, paid a $2,500 penalty, and personally reimbursed the Foundation for the $25,000, according to a Trump Organization official. The official described the reporting error as unintentional. These details document a prohibited political contribution and its correction, alongside the timing of Bondi’s decision. They do not establish that Trump and Bondi made an agreement to exchange the payment for a decision not to investigate.

preserved_fields.title: Donald Trump uses Trump Foundation to bribe Florida Attorney General
preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump uses Trump Foundation to bribe Florida Attorney General

notes: needs_context: the archived Washington Post report identifies the $25,000 2013 contribution, Bondi’s pending consideration and decision not to pursue the case, and the Foundation’s reimbursement and $2,500 IRS penalty. It does not establish a quid pro quo or give the payment’s exact date, so the title’s bribery claim remains unsupported.
